newsitem.title: USA: Silverado to buy La Teko's Ryan Lode.
newsitem.headline: Silverado to buy La Teko's Ryan Lode.

text.p: Silverado Gold Mines Ltd said Wednesday it has agreed with La Teko Resources Ltd to complete a U.S. $12 million, five year buyout of the Ryan Lode Property situated eight miles west of Fairbanks.
Preliminary cash flow analysis indicate production of 235 ounces of gold per day at a cost of under $200 per ounce.
Silverado said its due diligence examination of the property is expected to last about 60 days.
On completion, Silverado said, it will begin a drilling program to assess and determine the nature of the high grade gold bearing systems in the main ore body.
The property contains a known gold reserve of 742,500 proven ounces and 79,500 probable ounces, Silverado said.
Consisting of 63 federal and state claims totaling 1123 acres or nearly two square miles, it lies contiguous to Silverado's 20 square mile Ester Dome Property.
Silverado said the cash flow analysis is based on expectations operations will run at 1,000 tons per day of open pit mining and conventional gravity and CIP milling.
This acquisition is viewed by Silverado as the final step in its 26 year quest to become a significant North American Gold Producer, the company said.

Based on Silverado's past 17 years of operating experience on Ester Dome, the company said, "we believe that the Ryan Lode gold deposit is an important addition to Silverado's ore resources on Ester Dome."

Its statement continued: "We have built an infrastructure upon which we may continue to build as we become a sustainable producer of gold bullion. Based on our knowledge of the Ryan Lode ore body, we believe that it can supply a steady tonnage and grade of ore to the Grant Mill facilities, during which time we will add new reserves from the prior test mined O'Dea, Ethel, Elms, Silver Dollar and Ready Bullion ore bodies, as well as the presently developing St. Paul ore body.

"Our capital cost requirements for production will be relatively low, due to the fact that we have an existing 300 (ton per day) mill which is located one mile from the Ryan Lode ore body. It can be expanded to a greater capacity for substantially less cost than a new construction project.
"With the recent upgrade of the Golden Valley Electric System, we now will be able to purchase dependable power rather than generate our own power as we did in the past."
